blocks.text: The very first time I went to Hong Kong, I wasn’t really there to see the place. I remember that it was a business trip, the kind where a destination becomes a sequence of airports, hotel lobbies, meeting rooms, and haphazard meals squeezed between appointments. I remember arriving with a fairly conventional idea of what Hong Kong would be like: a vertical city of glass and concrete, neon-lit streets, crowded markets, shopping bags, and that famous skyline stretching across Victoria Harbour.
